title: Localization of a continuous site morphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be continuous and define a morphism of sites $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$: the sheaf functor $f_*G(T)=G(u(T))$ has a left adjoint $f^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For $V\in\mathcal D$ and $U=u(V)$ give $\mathcal D/V$ and $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topologies [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The functor $u_V:\mathcal D/V\to\mathcal C/U$, $(T\to V)\mapsto(u(T)\to U)$, is continuous and its induced sheaf inverse image preserves finite limits, hence defines a morphism of sites $f_V:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal D/V$. Write $j_U,j_V$ for the localization morphisms of topoi, whose inverse images are restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and whose direct images are their right adjoints. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$ (f_V)^{-1}j_V^{-1}\cong j_U^{-1}f^{-1},\qquad j_V^{-1}f_*\cong(f_V)_*j_U^{-1}. $$

proof.text: A covering in $\mathcal D/V$ is a covering in $\mathcal D$ with all arrows over $V$. Its image under $u_V$ is a covering in $\mathcal C/U$ because $u$ preserves coverings. The pullback of a covering arrow along an arrow over $V$ is its underlying pullback in $\mathcal D$, equipped with the induced map to $V$; continuity of $u$ identifies its image with the corresponding pullback over $U$. Thus $u_V$ satisfies both continuity conditions. The cited adjunction supplies $L_V\dashv R_V$, where $R_V=(f_V)_*$ is precomposition with $u_V$. For a sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C$ and $a:T\to V$, both $(j_V^{-1}f_*G)(a)$ and $(R_Vj_U^{-1}G)(a)$ are $G(u(T))$, with the same restriction and natural-transformation maps. This gives the canonical direct-image comparison, before any assertion of left exactness.

source.place: Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism, first paragraph of proof; continuity definitions 00WV, 00WX

proof.text:
Put $L=f^{-1}$ and $R=f_*$. Let $A=h_V^\#$ and $B=h_U^\#$, where $h_V(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(T,V)$ and $h_U(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,U)$. Sheafification, the adjunction $L\dashv R$ and the general Yoneda bijection give, naturally in $G\in\Sh(\mathcal C)$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(LA,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,RG)\cong RG(V)=G(U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,G).$$
The cited covariant Yoneda result gives an isomorphism $\theta:B\to LA$; take its inverse $c:LA\to B$. Equivalently, $c$ is the element of $\operatorname{Hom}(LA,B)$ corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_B$ under the displayed bijection at $G=B$. The adjoint $t:A\to RB$ of $c$ has, on a representable section $a:T\to V$, value $\eta_U(u(a))$ in $B(u(T))$: the displayed Hom bijection is evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_V$, and naturality in $T$ restricts this section along $u(a)$. This specifies the unit map used below even when the topology is not subcanonical.

source.place: Tag 04D3, lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf, proved here from its universal property; used in 03CF

proof.text:
Use the equivalences $E_V$ and $E_U$ of the cited localized-sheaves lemma. Define $\overline L:\Sh(\mathcal D)/A\to\Sh(\mathcal C)/B$ by $(H\xrightarrow p A)\mapsto(LH\xrightarrow{c\circ Lp}B)$. Its right adjoint sends $(G\xrightarrow q B)$ to
$$\overline R(G,q)=(RG\times_{RB} A\to A),$$
where the maps to $RB$ are $Rq$ and $t$. The pullback is a sheaf and is computed sectionwise by the cited limits result. Indeed a map $LH\to G$ over $B$ corresponds under $L\dashv R$ to a map $H\to RG$ satisfying $Rq\circ\alpha=t\circ p$; pairing it with $p$ gives exactly a map $H\to RG\times_{RB}A$ over $A$, and projection reverses this operation. All bijections are natural. At $a:T\to V$, the fibre description of $E_V^{-1}\overline R(G,q)$ is
$$\{s\in G(u(T)):q_{u(T)}(s)=t_T(\eta_V(a))\}=\{s\in G(u(T)):q_{u(T)}(s)=\eta_U(u(a))\}.$$
This is exactly $(R_V E_U^{-1}(G,q))(a)$, including the restriction maps. Consequently $E_U^{-1}\overline L E_V$ and $L_V$ are left adjoints of the same functor $R_V$. Their adjunction Hom bijections, followed by the cited covariant Yoneda result, yield a natural isomorphism $L_V\cong E_U^{-1}\overline L E_V$.

source.place: Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism, middle diagram and description of localized inverse image; adjunction calculation elaborates this description

proof.text: The final object of $\Sh(\mathcal D)/A$ is $\mathrm{id}_A$, carried by $\overline L$ to $c:LA\xrightarrow{\sim}B$, a final object of $\Sh(\mathcal C)/B$. A pullback over $A$ of $H_1\to H_0\leftarrow H_2$ has underlying sheaf $H_1\times_{H_0}H_2$ with its induced map to $A$. Since $L$ preserves finite limits by hypothesis, its image with the map induced by $c$ is the pullback over $B$ of the image span. Thus $\overline L$ preserves terminal objects and pullbacks, and hence finite limits: products are pullbacks over the terminal object and equalizers are the pullback of the diagonal along the pair of maps. Explicitly, the limit of a finite diagram $M:I\to\Sh(\mathcal D)/A$ is the equalizer of the two maps $\prod_{i\in\operatorname{Ob}(I)}M(i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{a:i\to j}M(j)$ whose $a$-components are respectively $M(a)\circ\mathrm{pr}_i$ and $\mathrm{pr}_j$; the equalizer equations are exactly the cone equations. Empty products are terminal objects. Thus the preceding constructions prove preservation for every finite diagram, including the empty one. Equivalences preserve and reflect these universal properties by their inverse Hom bijections, so the isomorphism in step 3 proves that $L_V$ preserves finite limits. With step 1 this makes $u_V$ a morphism of sites $f_V$, whose inverse image is $L_V$. To check the finite-colimit part of exactness in the cited definition, let $Q$ be a colimit of any finite diagram $M$ on the localized site. The adjunction $L_V\dashv R_V$ identifies maps $L_VQ\to G$ with maps $Q\to R_VG$, hence with compatible families $M(i)\to R_VG$, hence with compatible families $L_VM(i)\to G$. This is the colimit universal property for $L_VQ$, naturally in $G$; therefore $L_V$ also preserves finite colimits.

source.place: Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism, finite-limit argument after the middle diagram

proof.text: For any sheaf $K$ on $\mathcal D$, the quasi-inverse fibre formula identifies $E_V(j_V^{-1}K)$ with $(K\times A\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}A)$: its fibre at $a:T\to V$ consists of pairs $(s,\eta_V(a))$, naturally bijective to $K(T)$. Applying $\overline L$ and the product-preservation hypothesis identifies this object with $(LK\times B\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}B)$ using $c:LA\cong B$. Its image under $E_U^{-1}$ has at $b:X\to U$ fibre consisting of pairs $(s,\eta_U(b))$, naturally bijective to $LK(X)$, which is $j_U^{-1}LK$. The restriction maps send $s$ to its restriction, and a morphism $K\to K'$ acts by its image under $L$ on the first coordinate. Combining this natural identification with step 3 proves $(f_V)^{-1}j_V^{-1}\cong j_U^{-1}f^{-1}$. Together with step 1, these are precisely both required comparisons.
